title: Data Handling: Interpretation and Critical Analysis
summary: Interpreting real-world data and graphs, comparing groups with measures of centre and spread, box-and-whisker plots, scatter plots and trends, and critically evaluating claims and misleading representations.

rows: Compare medians and IQRs, or draw two box-and-whisker plots
Is there a relationship between two variables?

notes.text: A **percentile** tells you the percentage of data values below a value. A baby at the **75th percentile** for mass is heavier than 75% of babies of the same age. $Q_1$ is the 25th percentile and $Q_3$ the 75th.
A **scatter plot** shows pairs of values. A **trend line** (line of best fit) summarises the relationship and can be used to make predictions within the range of the data.

notes.title: Worked example 1
notes.problem: A scatter plot of hours of TV watched per day against test marks for 30 learners shows points falling from left to right. Describe the relationship and comment on a claim that 'TV makes you fail'.
steps: There is a negative relationship: learners who watch more TV tend to get lower marks.
However, correlation does not prove causation: other factors (study time, sleep, home support) may explain both.
A sample of 30 learners is small and may not represent all learners.
notes.answer: Negative correlation, but the claim is not proven.

items: **Who** collected the data and **why**? Could they be biased (e.g. a company reporting on its own product)?
**How big** and **how representative** was the sample?
Do the **axes** start at zero? Are the intervals equal?
Is a **trend** being extrapolated too far into the future?

notes.title: Worked example 2: comparing averages
notes.problem: Company A advertises 'average salary R32 000'. Salaries: 12 staff at R14 000, 3 managers at R45 000 and the owner at R190 000. Is the advert fair?
steps: The mean is pulled up by a few high earners, so the advert is misleading.
notes.answer: Not fair: the median R14 000 is more typical.

questions.prompt: A learner's mark is at the 90th percentile. This means…
options: she did better than about 90% of learners

questions.prompt: The lower quartile is the same as the…
In a negative relationship, as one variable increases the other tends to decrease.
Monthly rents in a block of flats: R4 200; R4 500; R4 500; R4 800; R5 100; R12 000. Find the median rent.
Find the mean rent for the same data (two decimals).
Which average (mean or median) better describes a typical rent in the block of flats above? Explain.
questions.memo:
✓ The median (1)
✓ The R12 000 penthouse is an outlier that raises the mean (1)

questions.prompt: School A: median 58%, IQR 24. School B: median 63%, IQR 10. Compare the two schools' results.
questions.memo:
✓ School B performed better on average (higher median) (2)
✓ School B's results are more consistent (smaller IQR) (1)
✓ School A has a wider spread of marks (1)

questions.prompt: A cool-drink company's survey of 50 of its customers finds that '9 out of 10 people prefer our drink'. Give THREE reasons to question this claim.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): sample is small; only the company's own customers (biased); company has an interest in the result; question wording unknown; no actual numbers/methods given

questions.prompt: A trend line shows the population of a town growing by 2 000 people per year from 2015 to 2024. Why is it risky to use it to predict the population in 2060?
questions.memo:
✓ 2060 is far outside the data range (extrapolation) (1)
✓ Growth rates can change because of economic, social or migration factors (1)

questions.prompt: Give TWO ways a graph can be made to look misleading.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): vertical axis not starting at zero; uneven scales; 3D effects; missing labels; cherry-picked time period
